utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-73-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ivan Cermak, and Mladen Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We're together for a Status Conference this afternoon. I would inquire first whether, Mr. Cermak, you are able to hear what is being said in a language you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERMAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Markac, are you able to understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MARKAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, you appear?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I do together with Laurie Sartorio, trial attorney, and case manager Lakshmie Walpita.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And counsel for Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm Cedo Prodanovic. Together with me is Mrs. Jadranka Slokovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am Miroslav Ceparovic, representative of Mr. Markac. My co-counsel is Goran Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The parties will be aware that the pre-trial management of this case has been assigned to me, and the reason for calling you together today is because of the requirement of the Rules is for Status Conferences to be held at least every 120 days. So it was convenient that you come together today to ensure that requirement was met. Now, I'm aware of only two matters that require specific attention. The first concerns the requirement of the Rules as to disclosure by the Prosecutor. There seemed a little earlier to be some perhaps misunderstanding as to when that requirement was satisfied. I think we've managed to clear that up. Do I now understand, Mr. Ierace, that you understand that you have completed your disclosure obligations?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Pursuant to 66(A)(i), we have, Your Honour, as of the 3rd of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Is there any disagreement with that by either Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no disagreement. I would like to point out that according to your ruling dated the 26th May, on the 16th of June the Prosecutor informed both us and yourselves that -- that they had disclosed the supportive materials on the 3rd of June, as my learned friend has stated. So we believe that the deadline for objection will start on the 16th of June, when we were informed about that. That's why we would like you to make a ruling to that effect. We base this position on Rule 72 in connection with Rule 66. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Rule 72 you referred to. What particular part of the Rule did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Article 72(A) and (B) paragraph (ii) are the ones that I had in mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I must say that I had understood it that it wasn't a matter of you being given a formal notice of completion of disclosure, but in this case disclosure was complete except for one matter, and that one matter was provided on the 3rd of June. I had myself been of the view that the time period would run from then. I don't immediately see anything in the Rule that would suggest that it wouldn't run until you received a notification that the disclosure had been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we were not in a position to know when they started running, because before the 16th of June, the Prosecution had not informed us that they had submitted supportive materials. And only in that letter, they informed us that they did it on the 3rd of June. They could have informed us that they had done it two months before that, which means that our deadline would have expired. I'm saying this because the supporting materials were not delivered to us in one go. It was done successively. It was only on our insistence that you made a ruling on the 26th of May and ordered the Prosecutor to inform us as to when their obligation was finally met, and this was done on the part of the Prosecution on the 16th of June. And it was on that day that we learned that the Prosecution would cease to submit any further supporting materials, and that is why we believed that the time for objection against this would start running on that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please remind me, am I correct in my recollection that the only outstanding matter was an English language translation of a document that you already had in Serbo-Croatian, or the other way around?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, surely you knew when you got that Serbo-Croatian translation that that then was the completion of the disclosure process.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we didn't know it, Your Honour, because the Prosecution had failed to inform us of that. Since documents were sent to us in batches. It was our position that there would be something else sent. That is what we assumed, and that is why we asked you, Your Honours, to make a ruling to order the Prosecution to inform us as to when we actually receive the last batch of the supporting materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there a reason why you couldn't look at the document and see that you had the complete document?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, we had an interview with the Prosecutor. We were preparing for that interview, and the Croatian translation was very important to us, this interview that General Markac with the Prosecution during the investigation. This would serve for our client to be informed about the contents of the interview. He could not do anything before he received the Croatian translation of the transcript, and as soon as he received that, he could prepare himself for the interview with the Prosecution that has taken place in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prodanovic, do you have any view on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The position of this Defence team is identical to the position put forward by my colleague Ceparovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I met with the -- both counsel for the Defence in relation to Mr. Markac on Thursday, the 10th of June, and they were informed at that point personally that disclosure was complete. They asked that we confirm it in writing, and we did. I might indicate, though, Your Honour, that for the part of the Prosecution, we don't take any particular position in relation to the application by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean you're happy for me on this occasion to take the, what was it, the 15th --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- 16th as the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that's a very graceful position, Mr. Ierace. You have one good success today. 16th of July becomes the date. Well, the two matters that I was aware of was both to ensure that everybody agreed that disclosure was complete and to be sure about the date by which preliminary motions would have to be filed. Well, that date is now the 16th of July. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I'm not aware of any other pending motions. Are there any that have escaped my attention? It seems to be none. Good. Perhaps counsel for each accused could tell me whether there is any matter which either accused would like to raise concerning matters of their health or the conditions of their detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ivan Cermak, although his health is somewhat impaired of which the -- Your Honour has been informed, currently doesn't have any health problems, nor he complains in any way about the conditions in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Prodanovic. Yes, Mr. Ceparovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Markac does not have any objections to the treatment that he's receiving in the Detention Unit. However, he has serious health problems due to his high blood sugar level, which is as high as 22, despite the medication that he has received. This is at the limit which seriously threatens his life. And if you wish, he can inform you of the details of his health condition. What I would like to point out, that even with the highest -- highest doses of medication, he can lower his blood sugar level to 12 or 13. And this is what we consider a serious health problem, and I believe that in the future we will have to consider a different medical treatment for our client. If you so wish, the general may give you some details of his health condition at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I really don't think I need to trouble your client, Mr. Ceparovic. The condition is known, and it's under medical observation and treatment, and clearly, if there is a matter that concerns your client, it should be taken up with the doctor that's managing his treatment, and those levels which you quote are matters that could be raised with the doctor if your client feels that there should be some increase of the present medication or change in the medication that he's receiving. I don't think it would help anybody for him to explain it to me. He'd better explain it to the doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I am grateful for you all to have come today. That completes the requirements of the Rules, and we're now about to get under way in the formal steps toward readying the evidence in the case for trial, and we'll be monitoring that as soon as we get past the 16th of July. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I bring one matter to your attention, which is that the Defence for General Markac has activated what used to be called reciprocal disclosure pursuant to Rule 66(B), and I understand from the Defence that in due course they will outline the categories of material which they wish to inspect pursuant to that Rule. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, that being so, we will adjourn now. Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: at 2.59 p.m.
